refs.quote: ZITHROMAX is a macrolide antibacterial drug indicated for the treatment of the following infections caused by designated susceptible microorganisms:

tall_man.note: Not listed in FDA/ISMP Tall Man list; generic name lowercase per EXTRACTION.md

regimens.indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) — Adults requiring initial IV therapy

refs.quote: The recommended dosage of ZITHROMAX for injection for the treatment of adult patients with community-acquired pneumonia due to the indicated organisms is 500 mg as a single daily dose by the intravenous route for at least two days.

dose.frequency: once daily for at least 2 days (infuse 1 mg/mL over 3 hr or 2 mg/mL over 1 hr)

infusion.diluent: 0.9% NaCl, 0.45% NaCl, D5W, Lactated Ringer's, or Normosol-M/R in D5W

regimens.dose_text: 500 mg IV once daily for at least 2 days (infuse at 1 mg/mL over 3 hours or 2 mg/mL over 1 hour; do not give as bolus or IM), followed by oral azithromycin 500 mg once daily to complete a 7- to 10-day course.

regimens.indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) — Oral step-down therapy in adults

refs.quote: Intravenous therapy should be followed by azithromycin by the oral route at a single, daily dose of 500 mg, administered as two 250 mg tablets to complete a 7- to 10-day course of therapy.

dose.frequency: once daily to complete 7- to 10-day total course

regimens.dose_text: 500 mg PO once daily (administered as two 250 mg tablets) following at least 2 days of IV therapy to complete a 7- to 10-day total course.

regimens.indication: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) — Adults requiring initial IV therapy

refs.locator: 2.2 Recommended Dosage for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
refs.quote: The recommended dosage of ZITHROMAX for injection for the treatment of adult patients with pelvic inflammatory disease due to the indicated organisms is 500 mg as a single daily dose by the intravenous route for one or two days.

dose.frequency: once daily for 1 to 2 days (infuse 1 mg/mL over 3 hr or 2 mg/mL over 1 hr)

infusion.diluent: 0.9% NaCl, 0.45% NaCl, D5W, Lactated Ringer's, or Normosol-M/R in D5W

regimens.dose_text: 500 mg IV once daily for 1 or 2 days, followed by oral azithromycin 250 mg once daily to complete a 7-day course. Add anaerobic coverage if anaerobes are suspected.

regimens.indication: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) — Oral step-down therapy in adults

refs.locator: 2.2 Recommended Dosage for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
refs.quote: Intravenous therapy should be followed by azithromycin by the oral route at a single, daily dose of 250 mg to complete a 7-day course of therapy.

dose.frequency: once daily to complete 7-day total course

regimens.dose_text: 250 mg PO once daily following 1 to 2 days of IV therapy to complete a 7-day total course.

refs.quote: Cardiovascular: Arrhythmias including ventricular tachycardia and hypotension. There have been reports of QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, and cardiovascular death.
Liver/biliary: Abnormal liver function, hepatitis, cholestatic jaundice, hepatic necrosis, and hepatic failure.
Skin/appendages: Pruritus, serious skin reactions including, erythema multiforme, AGEP, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, and DRESS.

mechanism_of_action.value: Macrolide (azalide) antibacterial that binds to the 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis and impeding 50S ribosomal subunit assembly.

refs.quote: Azithromycin acts by binding to the 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis and impeding the assembly of the 50S ribosomal subunit.
Co-administration of azithromycin increased the QTc interval in a dose- and concentration- dependent manner.

value.effect: Co-administration of nelfinavir at steady-state with a single oral dose of azithromycin increased azithromycin Cmax (2.36-fold) and AUC (2.12-fold).
value.management: Dose adjustment of azithromycin is not recommended, but close monitoring for known adverse reactions (liver enzyme abnormalities, hearing impairment) is warranted.

refs.quote: Although a dose adjustment of azithromycin is not recommended when administered in combination with nelfinavir, close monitoring for known adverse reactions of azithromycin, such as liver enzyme abnormalities and hearing impairment, is warranted.

value.effect: Spontaneous postmarketing reports suggest concomitant azithromycin may potentiate the effects of oral anticoagulants such as warfarin.
value.management: Carefully monitor prothrombin times while patients are receiving azithromycin and oral anticoagulants concomitantly.

refs.quote: Spontaneous postmarketing reports suggest that concomitant administration of azithromycin may potentiate the effects of oral anticoagulants such as warfarin, although the prothrombin time was not affected in the dedicated drug interaction study with azithromycin and warfarin.

value.effect: Drug interactions have been observed with other macrolide products, though not reported in clinical trials with azithromycin.
value.management: Careful monitoring of patients is advised when digoxin, colchicine, or phenytoin are used with azithromycin.

Available data from published literature and postmarketing experience over several decades with azithromycin use in pregnant women have not identified any drug-associated risks for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes (see Data ).
Limitations of these data include the lack of randomization and inability to control for confounders such as underlying maternal disease and maternal use of concomitant medications.

contraception.value: Does not reduce systemic hormonal contraceptive levels; backup contraception needed only if severe GI upset impairs pill absorption.

refs.quote: Unlike rifamycins, non-rifamycin beta-lactams, macrolides, glycopeptides, and fluoroquinolones do not reduce systemic ethinylestradiol or progestin levels; extra backup contraception is only required if severe antibiotic-associated vomiting or diarrhea impairs pill absorption.
